findings.explanation: Sources are queried in PropertySources iteration order, without consulting containsProperty; the first source whose getProperty(key) returns a non-null raw value wins. A null raw result advances to the next source, and a null source collection or all-null results produce null. Once a non-null raw value is found, nested processing, logging, and conversion occur and the method returns that result—even if conversion returns null—so lower-priority sources are not tried. There is no catch: an exception from a PropertySource or any subsequent processing propagates immediately and also prevents later-source lookup. The resolver does not cache property values or converted results; each lookup scans the current sources again, subject to any caching a custom source may perform itself.

Ordinary String and typed lookups enable nested-placeholder processing. A retrieved String is eligible for it for every target type. A non-String CharSequence is eligible only when the requested type is exactly String or CharSequence, and is first changed to String; other values, including a CharSequence requested as StringBuilder, bypass placeholder processing. Processing order is source retrieval, eligible nested-placeholder resolution, logKeyFound, then conversion to the requested type. Placeholder callbacks use getPropertyAsRawString, which rescans the same ordered sources with automatic nested processing disabled but still converts the selected value to String; the placeholder parser itself handles recursive substitution. Thus “raw” means no automatic nested pass, not no conversion or direct return of the source object.

Automatic resolution inside a property value is strict by default because ignoreUnresolvableNestedPlaceholders initially is false; setting it true selects non-strict handling. This nested path returns an empty String unchanged. Independently of that setting, explicit resolvePlaceholders always uses a non-strict helper, while resolveRequiredPlaceholders always uses a strict helper. Explicit empty text is also returned unchanged because the parser finds no placeholder; null text is rejected with IllegalArgumentException. Non-strict mode suppresses only the unresolved-placeholder error by retaining unresolved placeholder text (after any available inline fallback has been considered). It does not suppress circular-reference errors, exceptions from property retrieval/conversion, or other processing exceptions. Strict unresolved and circular cases throw PlaceholderResolutionException.

The value entering this method is the post-placeholder value. A null target type returns that same object, and, while no resolver-specific service exists, an already assignable value is likewise retained without conversion. Otherwise the shared DefaultConversionService is used. setConversionService rejects null and stores the supplied ConfigurableConversionService; once present, it is used even for assignable values. getConversionService lazily creates, stores, and thereafter returns an independent DefaultConversionService rather than the shared instance, so merely calling it establishes the resolver-specific service used by later conversions. The shared fallback is not stored in the resolver. A conversion result, including null, is returned directly and is not cached. Conversion exceptions are not caught, so they abort lookup and no lower source is considered.

Ordinary and typed retrieval are nullable. Default-valued overloads perform the same complete lookup and return the supplied, already typed default only when its final result is null; the default is not converted. Consequently, if a non-null raw value from the winning source is processed or converted to null, lower sources are still skipped but the API default is used. Required overloads perform the same lookup and throw IllegalStateException only when its final result is null, including a null produced after finding a source value. None of these wrappers catches failures: placeholder, source, logging, or conversion exceptions propagate as-is, so neither an API default nor the required-property “not found” exception replaces such a failure.
